incumbent_comparison: First pass against the generic Scavenger housing treatment in Room A: broad blue and cream doors and reclaimed timber improve faction identity, but the connected roof profiles make the pair read as one duplex-like block at 64 inches.
next_action_hypothesis: Reduce the mesh to at most 17 inches wide, preserve the shared porch and broad door slabs, and separate the two roof shapes: give one cottage a shallow asymmetric canopy and the other a short lean-to with a visible canvas patch. Keep each roof edge and its corner supports visually distinct from the neighboring cottage.

observations.art_direction_fit: The blue and cream salvaged appliance doors, weathered boards, canvas and mismatched sheet metal fit the Scavenger faction; there are no Clockwork cues on the homes.
observations.close_up_quality: The close view shows a coherent, supported pair with visible boards and hardware; the roof profiles still transfer less clearly than the target.
observations.gameplay_readability: In the actual Room A 64-inch view the door colors register, but the two homes merge into a single duplex-like mass.
observations.geometric_detail: The close view shows timber posts, bracing, doors and windows; the 64-inch view loses the distinction between the two cottage structures.
observations.material_realism: Weathered timber, enamel doors and galvanized roofing separate in the close view, while most finer surface variation falls away at 64 inches.
observations.proportion: The pair fills the local envelope convincingly, but Godot measures 17.272 x 6.573 x 8.761 inches, exceeding the specified width by 0.272 inches.
observations.scale_fidelity: The candidate remains near the requested dimensions but fails the width bound at 17.272 inches; its 64-inch gameplay view also weakens the paired-home read.
observations.semantic_recognizability: At 64 inches the blue and cream appliance doors plus reclaimed timber signal Scavenger housing, though the pair reads as one duplex-like block.
observations.silhouette_quality: The close render has two roof heights, but in the Room A gameplay view their continuous sheet coverage merges into one broad roof silhouette.
observations.surface_variation: Broad blue and cream slabs and roof color patches survive close inspection, but the distinct patched lean-to treatment does not read at gameplay scale.
observations.technical_integration: Godot 4.7.2 imports the GLB and renders it through the review-only resolver in rooms/room_a.json. Validation reports 185 mesh surfaces, 49,948 triangles and no import errors; the measured width is over the brief.

close_inspection.evidence: The close Room A render shows timber posts, braces, visible door hardware, roof sheet edges and distinct surface materials.

edge_treatment.evidence: The close render shows eased appliance slabs, rounded timber edges and thin roof-sheet profiles.

hardware.evidence: Both doors have simple pulls and iron straps visible in the close Room A render.

joins.evidence: Posts, headers, diagonal braces and porch supports provide visible connections and load paths in the close view.

manufacturing_detail.evidence: At the 64-inch camera the roof sheets visually connect the two homes, hiding the target's separate canopy and lean-to construction.

material_response.evidence: Weathered timber, blue and cream enamel, canvas and galvanized sheets respond distinctly under Room A lighting.

surface_variation.evidence: Close inspection shows board-to-board color variation and patched roof materials.

thickness.evidence: The roof sheets, appliance slabs and shared porch boards show readable thickness at close range.

neutral_viewer_realism.evidence: The close render reads as assembled miniature housing with material variation and visible supports, rather than untextured placeholder forms.

photo_character.evidence: The ArtBrief has no photographic source requirement or reference image.

visual_transfer_diagnosis.corrective_action: Shorten the porch board span to fit the 17-inch envelope and separate the roof silhouettes in 3D: keep one shallow asymmetric sheet canopy and make the second a clearly lower, shorter lean-to with a broad canvas repair and visible corner supports. Preserve the door blocks and shared porch.
